2. That the revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed against the judgment and decree dated 16-2-2010 (decree signed on 2-3-2010) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj in other class Appeal No. 77 of 2009 affirming the judgment and decree dated 12-3-2009 (decree signed on 16-3-2009) passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sonargaon, Narayangonj, in other class Suit No. 112 of 2005. When the Civil Revision was filed there a was delay of 1,015 days, as such the petitioners filed an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay. 

 5. That the learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that the reasons of delay as stated above are bonafide and unintentional. The delay has been caused as because Government as a litigant cannot take a quick decision regarding a case like the private litigant. Many authorities are involved in a case of the Government and as a result sometimes it may happen that Government cannot arrange everything in time such as vokalatnama, filing cost and certified copy of the concerned case. Further he submits that the Government's interest is the public interest and collective interest. The view of our Apex Court regarding condonation of delay in respect of the Government as a petitioner has been considered with somewhat leniency and in the present case the delay was beyond the control of the petitioner Government. Unless the delay is condoned, the petitioner Government will suffer irreparable loss and injury. In support of his submission he cited a case of Anu Baia vs Upazila Nirbahi Officer Perojpur reported in 43 DLR 611, wherein it is held that 'Condonation of delay in a case filed by the Government and the State need to go by the limitation applicable to all, but if the case by the Government is delayed, some consideration need be allowed considering the fact that even in the case of filing appeals, the Government remains a slow moving juristic person.' 

 8. I have gone through the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act filed by the petitioners and given my profound attention to the submissions advanced by the learned Deputy Attorney-General of the Government of Bangladesh. 

 9. Now for the better understanding of section 5 of The Limitation Act, the said section is quoted below: 

 'Any appeal or application for a revision or a review of judgment or for leave to appeal or any other application to which this may be made applicable by or under any enactment for the time being in force, may be admitted after the period of limitation prescribed thereof, when the appellant or applicant satisfies the Court that he had sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal or making the application within such period.' 

 13. Further, in the case of Circle Officer, Sutrapur vs Mohammad reported in 43 DLR 84, it is held, that 'In dealing with an application under section 5 of The Limitation Act, in the case of the Government, public interest has to be duly considered and various authorities, formalities and complications are involved and, as such, Government require a longer time in making the decision and acting on it. If, on behalf of the Government, a reasonable explanation of delay is given, there is no reason why it should not be accepted.'
